stories.notes: Story has zero acceptance criteria and null spec — completely unelaborated. Live preview across GO, UP, MX platforms in a CMS is a complex feature requiring full requirements elaboration (openspec first) followed by testability, security, and edge-case hardening (speckit). High priority due to multi-platform scope and total lack of existing specification.

agentContributions.notes: Previous output rejected for missing verificationCriteria. Description names three concrete testable behaviours — preview token detection, draft endpoint resolution, published-content fallback — now captured as observable, black-box VCs that stop at our side of the Contentstack boundary.

Openspec delivered an empty acceptanceCriteria array (noted as a re-do after a prior rejection for missing verificationCriteria). I constructed the full AC set from the story description, which names three core behaviours: preview token detection, draft endpoint resolution, and published-content fallback. I added: AC-5 (malformed/empty token), AC-6 (expired/invalid token fallback), AC-7 (token not leaked in responses), AC-8 (page structure/SEO consistency), AC-9 (precedence when both cookie and query param present), AC-10 (linked content also resolves in preview), AC-11 (cross-site coverage for GO, UP, MX). File contents were unavailable — ACs are derived solely from the description and file paths listed in technicalNotes. Once the implementation files (useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, pageService.ts, etc.) are reviewed, ACs around token detection mechanism and link resolution may need refinement.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Pipeline broke down: openspec was assigned to elaborate requirements but delivered an empty acceptanceCriteria array (acceptanceChanged: false, splitCount: 0) despite claiming to have captured three testable behaviors as verification criteria. Speckit then compensated by constructing AC-5 through AC-11 from the story description alone — effectively performing openspec's job rather than reviewing its output. This is a pipeline order violation: speckit should review openspec's deliverables, not replace them. Additionally, AC numbering starts at AC-5 with no AC-1 through AC-4, indicating a gap or numbering artifact. Speckit explicitly notes implementation files (useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, pageService.ts) were never reviewed, so token detection mechanism and link resolution ACs may need refinement once actual code is examined. Both agents did not add non-overlapping value in the intended sequence. Human review needed to validate the constructed ACs against actual implementation and fill the AC-1–AC-4 gap.
